sub_branches.concept_or_rule: Axis of Symmetry & Mirror Half Overlap
step_by_step_procedure: A figure has line symmetry if an axis divides it into two mirror-image halves.
Folding along line of symmetry causes both halves to coincide perfectly.
formulas_and_identities: Reflection Condition: Point (x, y) maps to (-x, y) across y-axis
sub_branches.example_problem: An isosceles triangle has 1 line of symmetry (vertical altitude).

step_by_step_procedure: A regular polygon with n sides has equal sides and angles.
It possesses exactly n lines of reflection symmetry.
sub_branches.example_problem: Equilateral triangle (n=3) has 3 lines; Square (n=4) has 4 lines; Regular pentagon (n=5) has 5 lines.

step_by_step_procedure: A shape has rotational symmetry if it matches its original orientation after rotation < 360° around center point O.
Order n equals total matching orientations during a full 360° turn.
formulas_and_identities: Order n = Total matching positions in 360°
sub_branches.example_problem: A 4-blade windmill matches original position 4 times in 360° (Order 4).

step_by_step_procedure: Calculate smallest rotation angle = 360° / Order n.
360° MUST be an exact integer multiple of smallest rotation angle.

branches.theme: 9.3 Combined Symmetry in Cultural & Natural Objects

step_by_step_procedure: 24 equally spaced spokes divide 360° into 24 sectors.
Possesses 24 lines of reflection symmetry and rotational symmetry of Order 24.
sub_branches.example_problem: Rotate Ashoka Chakra by 15° -> Looks identical to original.

step_by_step_procedure: Diagonals divide rectangle into congruent triangles, BUT folding along diagonal causes vertices to overhang.
Conclude rectangle has only 2 lines of symmetry (midsegments), NOT 4.
sub_branches.example_problem: Fold rectangular sheet along diagonal: Opposite corners overhang.
